text:
vp-eng: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Two things we need clarified for the roadmap doc: 1) how do batching/cache/kernel changes interact (order, dependencies) during a rollout? 2) what measurable health gates will eng-sre use for automated rollback? Keep answers short — product and CS need wording for customers. @maya-eng-runtime @rachel-eng-ops

maya-eng-runtime: Short answer: treat kernels as orthogonal infra changes, batching and KV-cache as workload-level optimizations. Order we prefer: kernel can go first (performance base), then batching config (to exploit new perf), then KV-cache tuning. But we will support alternative order per-model if the model family needs it.

rachel-eng-ops: Ops notes: we'll gate each step on the same pass/fail signals. We recommend an initial low-traffic kernel canary, then a combined canary for batching+cache. If the kernel alone regresses correctness metrics, we abort before changing batching.

jamal-ml: From ML side: kernels change execution characteristics (memory, latency distribution). Batching policies depend on per-token latency tail. So we should capture per-seq-length histograms during kernel canary and use that to pick batching params for next step. Expect: kernel -> update batching -> validate cache hit patterns.

sophia-product: For customer-facing text we need a single-sentence summary and a short bulleted FAQ. Can we get a one-liner for "what to expect" and a short line for Dedicated pinning?

maya-eng-runtime: One-liner: "We roll out runtime optimizations (kernel, batching, cache) in staged canaries; customers can pin model variants or opt out of automatic updates for Dedicated plans." FAQ line: "If you pin a variant, you keep the older behavior; pinned routes won't receive automated kernel/batching updates until unpinned."

tanya-cs: Customer asks: will rolling out kernels increase cost for customers? Need a short answer for CS.

jamal-ml: Likely no immediate cost increase; often kernels reduce compute time so costs drop. But batching and cache changes can change per-token billing patterns (more efficient batching -> lower cost per token), so say "typically neutral or positive".

rachel-eng-ops: Health gates (proposal): p95 token-latency delta <= +7% absolute, error-rate delta <= +0.3% absolute, correctness diffs <= 0.1% high-level-sampling, no new OOMs or GPU resets. Failure of any gate for a sustained 30m window triggers automatic rollback.

maya-eng-runtime: Draft rollout snippet for docs (example policy):
```json
{
  "steps": [
    {"name": "kernel-canary", "traffic": 2, "min_hours": 6},
    {"name": "kernel-batching-validate", "traffic": 10, "min_hours": 24},
    {"name": "cache-tune", "traffic": 50, "min_hours": 48},
    {"name": "full-rollout", "traffic": 100, "min_hours": 24}
  ],
  "rollback_triggers": {"p95_pct_increase": 7, "error_rate_abs": 0.3, "correctness_sample_pct": 0.1},
  "dedicated_pin_support": true
}
```

ops-bot: schedule created: attn-tiling-v3-canary -> 2025-06-13 02:00 UTC (initial window 72h). Monitor dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/mon/attn-tiling-v3-canary

vp-eng: OK action items: eng-runtime publish a short rollout flowchart + the JSON snippet by EOD Wed; eng-ops add the rollback monitors + runbook; product + CS to get the one-liner and FAQ entry for the release notes. Tag me on PRs. :+1:
